title: Implement the Sign-in with Google
author: mathrmartins
original_issue_body:
## User Story:
As a user who prefers convenient authentication methods, I want to be able to sign in seamlessly with my Google account.

## Description:
As a user, I want the option to sign in or sign up using my Google account to streamline the authentication process. This requires implementing the Google OAuth Provider within the NextAuth.js configuration. Additionally, I expect to find a "Sign in with Google" button on the sign-in page. Clicking this button should initiate the sign-in process via Next.js Server Action.

During the sign-in process, upon clicking the "Sign in with Google" button, I expect to be redirected to the Google authentication page to enter my credentials. After completing the sign-in process, I should be redirected back to the application and logged in.

Moreover, I anticipate that the sign-in process with Google will seamlessly integrate with the API backend built on Nest.js, ensuring a smooth user experience. Additionally, I would appreciate the option to enable One Tap Sign-in with Google for even faster authentication.

In summary, this user story aims to provide users with the convenience of signing in and signing up using their Google accounts while ensuring a seamless and efficient authentication process.

## Requirements:
- [x] Implement the Google Provider in the NextAuth.js configuration.
- [x] Implement the Next.js Server Action to initiate the Sign-in with Google process.
- [x] Manage the Sign-in with Google process in the NextAuth.js sign-in callback.
- [x] Integrate the Sign-in with Google with the backend API (Nest.js).
- [x] #63
- [x] Create the "Sign in with Google" button with its variations as specified in the [Sign in with Google Branding Guidelines](https://developers.google.com/identity/branding-guidelines).
- [x] Add the "Sign in with Google" button on the sign-in page.
- [x] Add the "Sign up with Google" button on the sign-in page.

title: [Enhancement]: Automatically translate content to the one browser is running
author: tolstenko
original_issue_body:
### Request Type

New Feature

### 🚨 Problem statement, Use Case, or Opportunity

I teach in English, and most of my materials are in English, but I would like to have my content served in at least Portuguese because most of our access is coming from Brazil.

### 💡 Describe the ideal solution in your perspective

I think we could try to use LLAMA to translate the texts for us and cache the result. 

- We could use a lazy load approach, which does not block access to the content, serves it as is, but enqueue the content to be translated, and tell the user, the text is being translated.
- The following calls, we need to check if the data is on the queue so we don't queue the same content to be translated too much, if it is there, do anything, just render the original text and tell the user, the text is being translated. But if the translation is done and on the cache, it delivers the data translated.
- Once the translation finishes, we should cache it.

ideally, if it is automatically translated, we should warn the user about it.

We should offer ways to store human translated content too, but I have no idea on how to do it properly yet.

title: [Enhancement]: Improve CI/CD following our git flow process
author: tolstenko
original_issue_body:
### Request Type

New Feature

### 🚨 Problem statement, Use Case, or Opportunity

Our current flow is pretty rudimentary and error prone; we need better automation for it.

### 💡 Describe the ideal solution in your perspective

Description:

- the developers commit their changes at the develop branch;
- when something is ready to publish, a mantainer merges from develop to the main branch
- once the merge occurs and the workflow passes, the semantic-release-bot will run and generate another commit, changing the CHANGELOG.md file and placing a commit there starting with chore(release): major.minor.fix [skip-ci]
- there is no deploy branch, the CD machine will track the main and only deploy when it sees a commit message on main like chore(release): major.minor.fix [skip-ci]
- deployment only occurs if there is a commit starting with name chore(release)
- main branch is locked for spontaneous merges, only admins and mantainers are allowed to merge

original_issue_body:
# API Versioning Options Configuration

**GitHub Issue Template: Feature Request**

## User Story
As a software architect, I want to configure API versioning strategies through a structured options pattern, so that I can implement multiple versioning approaches (URL-based, header-based, query parameter-based) while maintaining backward compatibility and clear API evolution paths.

## Problem Statement
Current API systems lack a unified configuration approach for versioning strategies. Different versioning methods (URL segments, HTTP headers, query parameters) require different implementations, making it difficult to standardize versioning across the entire API surface. There's no centralized way to configure versioning behavior, default versions, or migration policies.

## Proposed Solution
Implement `ApiVersioningOptions` that provides a structured configuration for API versioning with support for multiple strategies and unified version management.

### Core Components:
- **Versioning Strategy Configuration**: Support for URL, header, and query parameter versioning
- **Default Version Management**: Configure default API versions and fallback behavior
- **Version Format Specification**: Support for semantic versioning, date-based versioning, or custom formats
- **Deprecation Policies**: Configure how deprecated versions are handled
- **Backward Compatibility**: Rules for maintaining compatibility across versions

### Technical Implementation:
```csharp
public class ApiVersioningOptions
{
    public VersioningStrategy Strategy { get; set; }
    public string DefaultVersion { get; set; }
    public VersionFormat Format { get; set; }
    public DeprecationPolicy DeprecationPolicy { get; set; }
    public BackwardCompatibilityRules CompatibilityRules { get; set; }
    public Dictionary<string, VersionConfiguration> VersionConfigurations { get; set; }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Support for URL-based versioning (e.g., `/api/v1/users`, `/api/v2/users`)
- [ ] Support for header-based versioning (e.g., `X-API-Version: 1.0`)
- [ ] Support for query parameter versioning (e.g., `?version=1.0`)
- [ ] Configure default version when no version is specified
- [ ] Support for semantic versioning (Major.Minor.Patch)
- [ ] Support for date-based versioning (YYYY-MM-DD)
- [ ] Configure deprecation warnings and sunset dates
- [ ] Automatic routing to appropriate version handlers
- [ ] Version compatibility matrix configuration
- [ ] Integration with OpenAPI/Swagger documentation
- [ ] Validation of version format consistency
- [ ] Support for pre-release versions (alpha, beta, rc)

## Technical Requirements
- Integration with ASP.NET Core API versioning middleware
- Support for multiple concurrent versions
- Thread-safe configuration loading
- Performance-optimized version resolution
- Comprehensive logging of version usage
- Metrics collection for version adoption tracking

## Dependencies
- ASP.NET Core framework
- API versioning middleware packages
- Configuration system integration
- OpenAPI documentation generation
- Logging and metrics infrastructure

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `ApiVersioningOptions` class implemented with full configuration support
- [ ] Integration with ASP.NET Core dependency injection
- [ ] Support for all three versioning strategies (URL, header, query)
- [ ] Default version configuration and fallback behavior
- [ ] Deprecation policy implementation with warnings
- [ ] Version format validation and consistency checks
- [ ] OpenAPI integration for multi-version documentation
- [ ] Comprehensive unit tests covering all versioning scenarios
- [ ] Integration tests with sample API endpoints
- [ ] Performance tests for version resolution overhead
- [ ] Documentation with configuration examples and best practices
- [ ] Migration guide for existing APIs

## Problem Statement

Current authentication configurations are scattered across multiple files and lack standardization. Different authentication schemes require different setup procedures, making it difficult to maintain consistent security policies, token validation rules, and authentication flows across the entire API surface.

## Proposed Solution

Implement `AuthenticationOptions` that provides a centralized configuration for multiple authentication schemes with unified token management, security policies, and authentication flow control.

- **Multi-Scheme Support**: JWT Bearer, OAuth2, API Keys, Basic Authentication configuration
- **Token Management**: JWT signing, validation, refresh token policies
- **Security Policies**: Password requirements, account lockout, two-factor authentication
- **Session Management**: Cookie-based sessions, sliding expiration, security headers
- **Integration Points**: External identity providers, custom authentication handlers

```csharp
public class AuthenticationOptions
{
    public JwtBearerOptions JwtBearer { get; set; }
```

# Problem Details Options Configuration

**GitHub Issue Template: Feature Request**

## User Story

As a software architect, I want to configure RFC 7807 Problem Details responses through a structured options pattern, so that I can provide consistent, standardized error responses across all API endpoints with proper HTTP status codes, error details, and debugging information.

## Problem Statement

Current error handling lacks standardization across API endpoints. Different controllers return inconsistent error formats, making it difficult for clients to parse and handle errors uniformly. There's no centralized way to configure error response formats, debugging information levels, or compliance with RFC 7807 Problem Details specification.

## Proposed Solution

Implement `ProblemDetailsOptions` that provides a structured configuration for RFC 7807 compliant error responses with customizable error formatting, debugging information, and client-friendly error details.

### Core Components

- **RFC 7807 Compliance**: Standard problem details format with type, title, status, detail, instance
- **Error Mapping Configuration**: Map exceptions to appropriate HTTP status codes and problem types
- **Debugging Information Control**: Configure what debugging information to include based on environment
- **Localization Support**: Multi-language error messages and descriptions
- **Custom Extension Points**: Add domain-specific error properties and metadata

### Technical Implementation

```csharp
public class ProblemDetailsOptions
{
    public bool IncludeExceptionDetails { get; set; }
    public Dictionary<Type, ProblemTypeMapping> ExceptionMappings { get; set; }
    public ProblemDetailsDefaults Defaults { get; set; }
    public LocalizationOptions Localization { get; set; }
    public Dictionary<string, object> CustomExtensions { get; set; }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Generate RFC 7807 compliant problem details responses
- [ ] Map common exceptions to appropriate HTTP status codes
- [ ] Configure debugging information inclusion based on environment
- [ ] Support for custom problem types and error categories
- [ ] Include correlation IDs for request tracing
- [ ] Localized error messages based on Accept-Language header
- [ ] Custom extension properties for domain-specific errors
- [ ] Consistent error response format across all endpoints
- [ ] Integration with model validation errors
- [ ] Support for multiple error instances in single response
- [ ] Configurable error detail levels (minimal, standard, detailed)
- [ ] Client-friendly error codes and descriptions

## Technical Requirements

- Integration with ASP.NET Core problem details middleware
- Support for custom exception-to-problem mappings
- Thread-safe configuration and error processing
- Performance-optimized error response generation
- Comprehensive logging of error occurrences
- Integration with localization infrastructure

## Dependencies

- ASP.NET Core framework
- Problem details middleware packages
- Localization infrastructure
- Logging and correlation ID systems
- Configuration system integration

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `ProblemDetailsOptions` class implemented with full configuration support

# Rate Limiting Options Configuration

**GitHub Issue Template: Feature Request**

## User Story

As a software architect, I want to configure rate limiting policies through a structured options pattern, so that I can implement throttling strategies per user, IP address, and endpoint with configurable limits, time windows, and penalty policies to protect API resources from abuse.

## Problem Statement

Current API systems lack comprehensive rate limiting capabilities. There's no centralized way to configure throttling policies, implement different limiting strategies (per user, per IP, per endpoint), or manage rate limit violations with appropriate penalties and recovery mechanisms.

## Proposed Solution

Implement `RateLimitingOptions` that provides a structured configuration for comprehensive rate limiting with multiple strategies, configurable policies, and integrated monitoring.

### Core Components

- **Multi-Strategy Support**: Per user, per IP, per endpoint, and global rate limiting
- **Time Window Configuration**: Fixed window, sliding window, and token bucket algorithms
- **Policy Management**: Configure limits, penalties, and recovery mechanisms
- **Storage Backends**: In-memory, Redis, and database-backed rate limiting
- **Monitoring Integration**: Metrics collection and alerting for rate limit violations

### Technical Implementation

```csharp
public class RateLimitingOptions
{
    public Dictionary<string, RateLimitPolicy> Policies { get; set; }
    public RateLimitingStrategy DefaultStrategy { get; set; }
    public StorageBackendOptions Storage { get; set; }
    public MonitoringOptions Monitoring { get; set; }
    public PenaltyConfiguration Penalties { get; set; }
}
```

- [ ] Configure rate limits per user with authenticated user identification
- [ ] Configure rate limits per IP address with IP detection and forwarding support
- [ ] Configure rate limits per API endpoint with different limits per operation
- [ ] Support for fixed window, sliding window, and token bucket algorithms
- [ ] Global rate limiting across all endpoints and users
- [ ] Configurable time windows (seconds, minutes, hours, days)
- [ ] Rate limit violation penalties (temporary blocks, progressive delays)
- [ ] Integration with Redis for distributed rate limiting
- [ ] In-memory rate limiting for single-instance scenarios

- [ ] Monitoring and alerting for rate limit violations

# Cryptographic Signing & Integrity Verification of Audit Records

**Request Type:** New Feature

## 👤 User Story

As a security administrator and compliance officer, I want cryptographic signing and integrity verification of audit records so that I can prove the authenticity and non-repudiation of audit events for regulatory compliance and forensic investigations.

## Route URL

`/api/audit/signing`

## 🚨 Problem Statement, Use Case, or Opportunity

Current audit systems lack cryptographic proof of authenticity, making it difficult to verify that audit records haven't been tampered with or forged. Without digital signatures, organizations cannot provide non-repudiation guarantees required for regulatory compliance and legal proceedings.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Implement comprehensive cryptographic signing and verification for audit records:

**Digital Signature Implementation:**

- RSA-2048 or ECDSA P-256 digital signatures for all audit records
- Hardware Security Module (HSM) integration for key management
- Automatic timestamping service integration for temporal integrity
- Multi-signature support for high-value operations requiring multiple approvals

**Key Management System:**

- Secure key generation, storage, and rotation procedures
- Certificate-based public key infrastructure (PKI) integration
- Key escrow and recovery mechanisms for long-term verification
- Role-based key access controls and audit trails for key usage

**Integrity Verification Framework:**

- Real-time signature verification on audit record retrieval
- Batch verification jobs for validating historical record signatures
- Certificate chain validation ensuring signing key authenticity
- Signature expiration handling and re-signing procedures for long-term storage

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Digital signature implementation using RSA-2048 or ECDSA P-256 for all audit records
- [ ] Hardware Security Module (HSM) integration for secure key storage and signing operations
- [ ] Automatic timestamping service integration providing temporal integrity proof

- [ ] Comprehensive key management system with generation, rotation, and escrow capabilities

- [ ] Real-time signature verification during audit record retrieval and access
- [ ] Batch verification jobs for validating signatures on historical audit records
- [ ] Certificate expiration handling with automatic re-signing for long-term preservation
- [ ] Non-repudiation guarantees ensuring signed records cannot be denied by signatories

## 📈 Impact, Risks and Benefits

**Benefits:**

- Legal non-repudiation ensuring audit records are admissible in court proceedings
- Regulatory compliance with digital signature requirements for audit trails
- Enhanced security through cryptographic proof of record authenticity
- Improved forensic capabilities with tamper-evident audit evidence

original_issue_body:
# Tamper-Evident Append-Only Audit Log Store

**Request Type:** New Feature

## 👤 User Story

As a compliance officer and security administrator, I want a tamper-evident append-only audit log store with WORM (Write Once, Read Many) capabilities and hash chain verification so that I can ensure the integrity and immutability of audit records for regulatory compliance and forensic investigations.

## Route URL

`/api/audit/tamper-evident`

## 🚨 Problem Statement, Use Case, or Opportunity

Current audit systems may be vulnerable to tampering, modification, or deletion of audit records, which can compromise forensic investigations and regulatory compliance. Without tamper-evident storage, organizations cannot prove the integrity of their audit trails to auditors or during legal proceedings.

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Implement a tamper-evident append-only audit log store with the following capabilities:

**WORM Storage Implementation:**
- Append-only data structure preventing modification or deletion of existing records
- Immutable storage layer with cryptographic protection
- Write-once semantics enforced at the database and application level

**Hash Chain Verification:**
- Each audit record contains a hash of the previous record, creating an unbreakable chain
- SHA-256 or stronger cryptographic hashing for record linking
- Merkle tree structures for efficient batch verification
- Periodic checkpoint hashes for long-term integrity validation

**Integrity Verification:**
- Real-time hash chain validation on record insertion
- Batch integrity verification jobs for historical records
- Tamper detection alerts when hash chain breaks are discovered
- Forensic analysis tools for investigating integrity violations

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Append-only audit log storage preventing modification or deletion of existing records
- [ ] Hash chain implementation linking each record to its predecessor with cryptographic hashes
- [ ] WORM storage semantics enforced at both database and application levels
- [ ] Real-time integrity verification during record insertion with hash validation
- [ ] Batch integrity verification jobs for validating historical audit record chains
- [ ] Tamper detection system generating alerts when hash chain inconsistencies are discovered
- [ ] Merkle tree implementation for efficient batch verification of large audit datasets
- [ ] Periodic checkpoint generation for long-term integrity validation and verification
- [ ] Forensic analysis tools for investigating and reporting integrity violations
- [ ] Performance optimization ensuring minimal impact on audit record insertion speed

## 📈 Impact, Risks and Benefits

**Benefits:**

- Regulatory compliance with SOX, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and other audit trail requirements
- Forensic integrity ensuring audit records can be trusted in legal proceedings
- Enhanced security posture with tamper-evident audit capabilities
- Improved confidence in audit data accuracy and completeness

**Risks:**

- Increased storage requirements due to immutable append-only design

**Google OAuth Example:**
```csharp
public class GoogleOAuthProvider : IOAuthProvider
{
    public async Task<OAuthUserInfo> GetUserInfoAsync(string code)
    {
        // Exchange code for token
        var tokenResponse = await ExchangeCodeAsync(code);
        
        // Verify ID token
        var payload = await GoogleJsonWebSignature.ValidateAsync(
            tokenResponse.IdToken);
        
        return new OAuthUserInfo
        {
            Email = payload.Email,
            EmailVerified = payload.EmailVerified,
            Name = payload.Name,
            Picture = payload.Picture,
            ProviderId = payload.Subject,
            Provider = OAuthProvider.Google
        };
    }
}
```

**Frontend Integration:**
```typescript
// Redirect to OAuth provider
const initiateOAuth = (provider: string) => {
  const state = generateRandomState();
  sessionStorage.setItem('oauth_state', state);
  
  window.location.href = `/api/auth/oauth/${provider}/authorize?` +
    `redirect_uri=${encodeURIComponent(window.location.origin + '/auth/callback')}` +
    `&state=${state}`;
};

// Handle callback
const handleCallback = async (code: string, state: string) => {
  const savedState = sessionStorage.getItem('oauth_state');
  if (state !== savedState) throw new Error('Invalid state');
  
  const response = await fetch('/api/auth/oauth/callback', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ code, state, provider })
  });
};
```

# API Versioning Options Configuration

**GitHub Issue Template: Feature Request**

## User Story
As a software architect, I want to configure API versioning strategies through a structured options pattern, so that I can implement multiple versioning approaches (URL-based, header-based, query parameter-based) while maintaining backward compatibility and clear API evolution paths.

## Problem Statement
Current API systems lack a unified configuration approach for versioning strategies. Different versioning methods (URL segments, HTTP headers, query parameters) require different implementations, making it difficult to standardize versioning across the entire API surface. There's no centralized way to configure versioning behavior, default versions, or migration policies.

## Proposed Solution
Implement `ApiVersioningOptions` that provides a structured configuration for API versioning with support for multiple strategies and unified version management.

### Core Components:
- **Versioning Strategy Configuration**: Support for URL, header, and query parameter versioning
- **Default Version Management**: Configure default API versions and fallback behavior
- **Version Format Specification**: Support for semantic versioning, date-based versioning, or custom formats
- **Deprecation Policies**: Configure how deprecated versions are handled
- **Backward Compatibility**: Rules for maintaining compatibility across versions

### Technical Implementation:
```csharp
public class ApiVersioningOptions
{
    public VersioningStrategy Strategy { get; set; }
    public string DefaultVersion { get; set; }
    public VersionFormat Format { get; set; }
    public DeprecationPolicy DeprecationPolicy { get; set; }
    public BackwardCompatibilityRules CompatibilityRules { get; set; }
    public Dictionary<string, VersionConfiguration> VersionConfigurations { get; set; }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Support for URL-based versioning (e.g., `/api/v1/users`, `/api/v2/users`)
- [ ] Support for header-based versioning (e.g., `X-API-Version: 1.0`)
- [ ] Support for query parameter versioning (e.g., `?version=1.0`)
- [ ] Configure default version when no version is specified
- [ ] Support for semantic versioning (Major.Minor.Patch)
- [ ] Support for date-based versioning (YYYY-MM-DD)
- [ ] Configure deprecation warnings and sunset dates
- [ ] Automatic routing to appropriate version handlers
- [ ] Version compatibility matrix configuration
- [ ] Integration with OpenAPI/Swagger documentation
- [ ] Validation of version format consistency
- [ ] Support for pre-release versions (alpha, beta, rc)

## Technical Requirements
- Integration with ASP.NET Core API versioning middleware
- Support for multiple concurrent versions

## Request Type
New Feature

## 👤 User Story
As a Web3 user, I want to authenticate using my crypto wallet (MetaMask, WalletConnect, Coinbase Wallet) so that I can access the platform without traditional credentials and maintain my blockchain identity.

## 🚨 Problem Statement, Use Case, or Opportunity
Web3 and blockchain gaming users expect wallet-based authentication:

**User Expectations:**
- No passwords required
- Wallet address as primary identity
- Sign messages to prove ownership
- NFT gating capabilities (future)
- Token-based access control (future)
- Blockchain transaction integration

**Platform Opportunities:**
- Native blockchain integration
- NFT marketplace authentication
- Token-gated content
- Crypto payment integration
- DAO governance participation
- On-chain reputation systems

**Current Gap:**
- No Web3 authentication support
- Blockchain users forced to use traditional auth
- Missing competitive feature for GameFi

## 💡 Proposed Solution
Implement EIP-191/EIP-712 message signing authentication:

**Supported Wallets:**
- MetaMask (browser extension)
- WalletConnect (mobile wallets)
- Coinbase Wallet
- Trust Wallet
- Rainbow Wallet
- Any EIP-1193 compatible wallet

**Authentication Flow:**
1. User connects wallet (request address)
2. Server generates challenge message with nonce
3. User signs message with private key (wallet popup)
4. Server verifies signature against address
5. JWT token issued for session

**Message Signing (EIP-191):**
```
Sign this message to authenticate with GameGuild:

Wallet: 0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f0bEb
Nonce: 8f3e7b2a-5c1d-4e9f-a6b3-7d2c8f1e4a9b
Issued At: 2025-10-02T15:30:00Z
Chain ID: 1

This request will not trigger a blockchain transaction or cost gas fees.
```

**Security Features:**
- Nonce-based replay protection
- Time-limited challenges (5 minutes)
- Chain ID validation
- Message format standardization
- Signature verification (ecrecover)
- Rate limiting per address

**Implementation:**
```csharp
public class Web3ChallengeCommand
{
    public string WalletAddress { get; set; }
}

public class Web3VerifyCommand
{
    public string WalletAddress { get; set; }
    public string Signature { get; set; }
    public string Message { get; set; }
    public string Nonce { get; set; }
}

// Signature verification
var recoveredAddress = EthereumMessageSigner.EncodeUTF8AndEcRecover(
    message, signature);
    
if (recoveredAddress.ToLower() != walletAddress.ToLower())
    throw new InvalidSignatureException();
```

**Account Linking:**
- Link wallet to existing email account
- Multiple wallets per account
- Primary wallet designation
- Wallet address display in profile

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Web3 challenge generation endpoint
- [ ] Nonce generation and storage
- [ ] Challenge message formatting (EIP-191)
- [ ] Signature verification implementation
- [ ] Wallet address validation (checksum)
- [ ] Chain ID validation
- [ ] Challenge expiration (5 minutes)
- [ ] Replay protection
- [ ] JWT token issuance after verification
- [ ] Account creation for new wallets
- [ ] Account linking to existing users
- [ ] Multiple wallet support per user
- [ ] Wallet disconnection
- [ ] Frontend wallet connection libraries
- [ ] MetaMask integration
- [ ] WalletConnect integration
- [ ] Rate limiting per wallet address
- [ ] Metrics for Web3 auth usage
- [ ] Documentation with integration guides
- [ ] Unit and integration tests

## 📈 Impact, Risks and Benefits

**Benefits:**
- Native Web3 user experience
- No password management
- Blockchain identity integration
- NFT/token gating foundation
- Competitive advantage in GameFi
- Future crypto payment integration
- On-chain reputation potential

**Risks:**
- Users losing wallet access (no recovery)
- Phishing attacks targeting signatures
- Wallet compatibility issues
- Gas-free verification (user confusion)
- Limited Web3 adoption currently
- Technical complexity

**Impact:**
- Critical for blockchain gaming features
- Differentiator in competitive market
- Foundation for NFT marketplace
- Required for token-gated content
- Enables future DAO features

## 📚 Context and Examples

**Frontend Integration (ethers.js):**
```typescript
import { ethers } from 'ethers';

// Request wallet connection
const connectWallet = async () => {
  const provider = new ethers.BrowserProvider(window.ethereum);
  const signer = await provider.getSigner();
  const address = await signer.getAddress();
  
  // Request challenge
  const challengeResponse = await fetch('/api/auth/web3/challenge', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ walletAddress: address })
  });
  
  const { message, nonce } = await challengeResponse.json();
  
  // Sign message
  const signature = await signer.signMessage(message);
  
  // Verify signature
  const verifyResponse = await fetch('/api/auth/web3/verify', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({
      walletAddress: address,
      signature,
      message,
      nonce
    })
  });
  
  const { token } = await verifyResponse.json();
  localStorage.setItem('auth_token', token);
};
```

**WalletConnect Integration:**
```typescript
import { WalletConnectConnector } from '@web3-react/walletconnect-connector';

const walletConnect = new WalletConnectConnector({
  rpc: { 1: 'https://mainnet.infura.io/v3/YOUR_KEY' },
  qrcode: true
});

await walletConnect.activate();
const account = await walletConnect.getAccount();
```

**Signature Verification (Backend):**
```csharp
using Nethereum.Signer;

public bool VerifySignature(string message, string signature, string address)
{
    var signer = new EthereumMessageSigner();
    var recoveredAddress = signer.EncodeUTF8AndEcRecover(message, signature);
    
    return string.Equals(
        recoveredAddress,
        address,
        StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
}
```

**Standards:**
- EIP-191: Signed Data Standard
- EIP-712: Typed structured data hashing and signing
- EIP-1193: Ethereum Provider JavaScript API
- EIP-1271: Standard Signature Validation (smart contracts)

## 🔧 Technical Requirements

- [x] Database schema changes required
- [x] Frontend changes required
- [x] Third-party integrations needed (Web3 libraries)
- [x] Documentation updates needed
- [x] Tests must be written

Related to authentication module and blockchain integration features

- Queries and mutations can expose unauthorized data

**Core Authorization Infrastructure:**
- `@authorize` directive for queries and mutations with permission requirements

- GraphQL middleware pipeline for authorization enforcement

**Implementation Components:**
- `DACAuthorizationMiddleware` for request-level authorization
- `AuthorizeDirectiveType` for schema-level permission declarations
- `GraphQLPermissionContext` for accessing user permissions during execution
- `PermissionBasedSchemaFilter` for dynamic schema generation
- Integration with existing DAC permission resolver

- [ ] Field-level authorization prevents unauthorized access to specific fields

- Reduced security vulnerabilities in complex nested queries

# DAC Permission Attributes System

As a developer, I want to use declarative authorization attributes on controllers and actions so that I can easily enforce DAC (Discretionary Access Control) permissions without writing repetitive authorization code in each endpoint.

## Problem Statement

Implementing authorization checks manually in each controller action leads to code duplication, inconsistent security enforcement, and increased risk of security vulnerabilities. Without a standardized attribute-based approach, developers must remember to implement permission checks correctly in every endpoint, leading to potential security gaps.

## Proposed Solution

Implement a comprehensive set of DAC permission attributes that can be applied declaratively to controllers and actions, providing automatic permission verification with support for tenant-level, content-type, and resource-level permissions, including multiple requirement logic and custom validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Core Attribute Implementation

- [ ] Implement `RequireDacPermissionAttribute` for tenant-level permission enforcement
- [ ] Create `RequireContentTypePermissionAttribute<T>` for content-type specific permissions
- [ ] Develop `RequireResourcePermissionAttribute<T>` for resource-level permissions with route extraction
- [ ] Support multiple permission requirements with AND logic combination
- [ ] Enable custom permission validation logic through extensible attribute framework

### Permission Parameter Handling

- [ ] Support PermissionType enumeration parameter binding
- [ ] Implement TenantId parameter resolution from route, claims, or context
- [ ] Create ResourceIdRoute parameter for dynamic resource ID extraction
- [ ] Support generic type parameters for strongly-typed content and resource permissions
- [ ] Enable flexible parameter binding from multiple sources (route, query, header, claims)

### Attribute Composition & Logic

- [ ] Allow multiple DAC attributes on single action with AND logic
- [ ] Support attribute inheritance from controller to action level
- [ ] Implement attribute precedence rules for conflicting permissions
- [ ] Enable conditional attribute application based on runtime context
- [ ] Support attribute composition for complex permission scenarios

- [ ] Support custom error response formatting

## Technical Requirements

### Attribute Framework

- Create base DAC attribute class with common functionality
- Implement attribute validation during application startup
- Support dependency injection within attribute constructors
- Design for extensibility with custom attribute implementations
- Ensure thread-safety for concurrent request processing

title: [FEATURE] Multi-Currency Pricing & FX Rate Synchronization
author: mathrmartins
original_issue_body:
## Request Type
Feature Request

## User Story
As a **SaaS platform administrator**, I want to **offer pricing in multiple currencies with automatic foreign exchange rate synchronization** so that **international customers can view prices and pay in their local currency, improving conversion rates and user experience**.

## Problem Statement
Current billing system only supports single-currency pricing (typically USD), forcing international customers to:
- Calculate conversion rates manually
- Pay foreign transaction fees on credit cards
- Deal with confusing pricing displays
- Experience price fluctuations due to FX rate changes

Global SaaS platforms need:
- Display prices in 150+ currencies
- Automatic FX rate updates from reliable providers
- Currency-specific rounding rules (JPY has no decimals, KWD has 3 decimals)
- Multi-currency revenue reporting and reconciliation
- Base currency for accounting with foreign currency tracking
- Price override capability per market (psychological pricing like $9.99 vs €8.99)
- Historical FX rate storage for audit and tax compliance
- Currency switching in user accounts without data loss

Without multi-currency support:
- Lost sales from international customers confused by foreign currency pricing
- Increased support burden explaining FX calculations
- Competitive disadvantage vs platforms offering local currency
- Complex manual accounting for multi-currency revenue
- Risk of pricing errors during currency fluctuations

## Proposed Solution

### Currency Configuration Entity
```csharp
public class CurrencyConfiguration
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public string CurrencyCode { get; set; } // ISO 4217: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, etc.
    public string DisplayName { get; set; } // "US Dollar", "Euro"
    public string Symbol { get; set; } // "$", "€", "£", "¥"
    public int DecimalPlaces { get; set; } // 2 for most, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD
    public bool IsEnabled { get; set; }
    public bool IsBaseCurrency { get; set; } // Accounting base (typically USD)
    public int DisplayOrder { get; set; }
    public DateTime EnabledAt { get; set; }
    public DateTime? DisabledAt { get; set; }
}
```

### Exchange Rate Entity
```csharp
public class ExchangeRate
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public string BaseCurrency { get; set; } // USD
    public string TargetCurrency { get; set; } // EUR
    public decimal Rate { get; set; } // 0.85 (1 USD = 0.85 EUR)
    public DateTime EffectiveDate { get; set; }
    public ExchangeRateSource Source { get; set; } // OpenExchangeRates, ECB, Manual
    public string Provider { get; set; } // API provider name
    public string RawResponse { get; set; } // JSON response from provider for audit
    public DateTime CreatedAt { get; set; }
}

public enum ExchangeRateSource
{
    OpenExchangeRates,
    ECB, // European Central Bank
    Manual,
    FixedOverride
}
```

### Price Localization Entity
```csharp
public class PriceLocalization
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public Guid PlanId { get; set; }
    public string CurrencyCode { get; set; }
    public decimal LocalizedPrice { get; set; } // Override price (e.g., €8.99 instead of €8.67)
    public bool IsAutoCalculated { get; set; } // true = use FX rate, false = manual override
    public DateTime? LastCalculatedAt { get; set; }
    public decimal? ExchangeRateUsed { get; set; } // Rate at time of last calculation
    public DateTime EffectiveDate { get; set; }
    public DateTime? ExpiryDate { get; set; }
}
```

### IExchangeRateService Interface
```csharp
public interface IExchangeRateService
{
    Task<decimal> GetCurrentRateAsync(string baseCurrency, string targetCurrency, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    Task<Dictionary<string, decimal>> GetAllRatesAsync(string baseCurrency, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    Task SyncRatesFromProviderAsync(ExchangeRateSource source, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    Task<ExchangeRate> GetHistoricalRateAsync(string baseCurrency, string targetCurrency, DateTime date, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    Task<decimal> ConvertAsync(decimal amount, string fromCurrency, string toCurrency, DateTime? date = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

### OpenExchangeRatesService Implementation
```csharp
public class OpenExchangeRatesService : IExchangeRateService
{
    private readonly HttpClient _httpClient;
    private readonly IConfiguration _configuration;
    private readonly ApplicationDbContext _context;
    
    public async Task SyncRatesFromProviderAsync(ExchangeRateSource source, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        if (source != ExchangeRateSource.OpenExchangeRates)
            throw new InvalidOperationException($"This service only supports {ExchangeRateSource.OpenExchangeRates}");
            
        var apiKey = _configuration["OpenExchangeRates:ApiKey"];
        var response = await _httpClient.GetAsync($"https://openexchangerates.org/api/latest.json?app_id={apiKey}", cancellationToken);
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
        
        var json = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cancellationToken);
        var data = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<OpenExchangeRatesResponse>(json);
        
        var baseCurrency = data.Base; // USD
        var effectiveDate = DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(data.Timestamp).UtcDateTime;
        
        var exchangeRates = new List<ExchangeRate>();
        foreach (var (currency, rate) in data.Rates)
        {
            exchangeRates.Add(new ExchangeRate
            {
                BaseCurrency = baseCurrency,
                TargetCurrency = currency,
                Rate = rate,
                EffectiveDate = effectiveDate,
                Source = ExchangeRateSource.OpenExchangeRates,
                Provider = "Open Exchange Rates",
                RawResponse = json,
                CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow
            });
        }
        
        await _context.ExchangeRates.AddRangeAsync(exchangeRates, cancellationToken);
        await _context.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
    }
    
    public async Task<decimal> ConvertAsync(decimal amount, string fromCurrency, string toCurrency, DateTime? date, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        if (fromCurrency == toCurrency)
            return amount;
            
        var rate = date.HasValue 
            ? await GetHistoricalRateAsync("USD", toCurrency, date.Value, cancellationToken)
            : await GetCurrentRateAsync("USD", toCurrency, cancellationToken);
            
        // If fromCurrency is not USD, need to convert via USD
        if (fromCurrency != "USD")
        {
            var fromRate = date.HasValue
                ? await GetHistoricalRateAsync("USD", fromCurrency, date.Value, cancellationToken)
                : await GetCurrentRateAsync("USD", fromCurrency, cancellationToken);
            return amount / fromRate.Rate * rate;
        }
        
        return amount * rate;
    }
}
```

### Commands
```csharp
// Configure currency
public record EnableCurrencyCommand(string CurrencyCode) : IRequest<Result>;
public record DisableCurrencyCommand(string CurrencyCode) : IRequest<Result>;
public record SetBaseCurrencyCommand(string CurrencyCode) : IRequest<Result>;

// Sync FX rates
public record SyncExchangeRatesCommand(ExchangeRateSource Source) : IRequest<Result<int>>; // Returns count synced
public record SetManualExchangeRateCommand(string BaseCurrency, string TargetCurrency, decimal Rate) : IRequest<Result>;

// Localized pricing
public record SetLocalizedPriceCommand(Guid PlanId, string CurrencyCode, decimal LocalizedPrice, bool IsManualOverride) : IRequest<Result>;
public record RecalculateLocalizedPricesCommand(Guid? PlanId = null) : IRequest<Result<int>>; // Recalc all or specific plan
```

### Queries
```csharp
public record GetEnabledCurrenciesQuery : IRequest<Result<List<CurrencyConfiguration>>>;
public record GetCurrentExchangeRateQuery(string BaseCurrency, string TargetCurrency) : IRequest<Result<decimal>>;
public record GetExchangeRateHistoryQuery(string BaseCurrency, string TargetCurrency, DateTime StartDate, DateTime EndDate) : IRequest<Result<List<ExchangeRate>>>;
public record GetLocalizedPriceQuery(Guid PlanId, string CurrencyCode) : IRequest<Result<decimal>>;
public record GetPlanPricingInAllCurrenciesQuery(Guid PlanId) : IRequest<Result<Dictionary<string, decimal>>>;
public record ConvertAmountQuery(decimal Amount, string FromCurrency, string ToCurrency, DateTime? Date = null) : IRequest<Result<decimal>>;
```

### REST API Endpoints
```csharp
// GET /api/currencies - List all enabled currencies
// POST /api/currencies/{code}/enable - Enable currency
// POST /api/currencies/{code}/disable - Disable currency
// PUT /api/currencies/base - Set base currency for accounting

// GET /api/exchange-rates/current?base=USD&target=EUR - Get current rate
// GET /api/exchange-rates/history?base=USD&target=EUR&start=2025-01-01&end=2025-12-31 - Historical rates
// POST /api/exchange-rates/sync - Trigger FX rate sync from provider
// POST /api/exchange-rates/manual - Set manual override rate

// GET /api/plans/{planId}/pricing/{currency} - Get localized price
// GET /api/plans/{planId}/pricing/all - Get prices in all currencies
// PUT /api/plans/{planId}/pricing/{currency} - Set manual localized price
// POST /api/plans/{planId}/pricing/recalculate - Recalculate auto prices

// POST /api/currency/convert - Convert amount between currencies
```

### Background Jobs
```csharp
// Daily FX Rate Sync (runs at 00:00 UTC)
public class DailyExchangeRateSyncJob : IJob
{
    public async Task Execute(IJobExecutionContext context)
    {
        await _mediator.Send(new SyncExchangeRatesCommand(ExchangeRateSource.OpenExchangeRates));
        await _mediator.Send(new RecalculateLocalizedPricesCommand()); // Update auto-calculated prices
    }
}

// Weekly Price Localization Audit (detect stale overrides)
public class PriceLocalizationAuditJob : IJob
{
    public async Task Execute(IJobExecutionContext context)
    {
        // Find manual overrides that differ significantly from auto-calculated prices
        // Alert admins to review pricing strategies
    }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

### Currency Management
- [ ] Support 150+ currencies (ISO 4217 standard)
- [ ] Enable/disable currencies via admin console
- [ ] Set one base currency for accounting (typically USD)
- [ ] Configure decimal places per currency (0 for JPY, 2 for USD, 3 for KWD)
- [ ] Display currency symbols and names correctly
- [ ] Validate currency codes against ISO 4217 standard
- [ ] Prevent disabling base currency
- [ ] Warn when disabling currency with active subscriptions

### Exchange Rate Synchronization
- [ ] Integrate with Open Exchange Rates API (primary provider)
- [ ] Support European Central Bank (ECB) as fallback provider
- [ ] Sync FX rates daily at 00:00 UTC automatically
- [ ] Store historical rates with effective dates
- [ ] Manual override capability for specific rates
- [ ] Audit log showing rate changes over time
- [ ] Cache current rates in Redis for 1 hour
- [ ] Retry failed sync attempts with exponential backoff
- [ ] Alert admins on 3 consecutive sync failures
- [ ] Store raw API responses for audit trail

### Price Localization
- [ ] Auto-calculate prices in all enabled currencies using current FX rates
- [ ] Support manual price overrides per market (psychological pricing)
- [ ] Display override vs auto-calculated price in admin UI
- [ ] Recalculate auto prices when FX rates update
- [ ] Preserve manual overrides during recalculation
- [ ] Effective date support for future price changes
- [ ] Expiry date for temporary price overrides
- [ ] Bulk recalculation with progress tracking
- [ ] Preview price changes before applying
- [ ] Rollback capability for price updates

### Currency Conversion
- [ ] Convert amounts between any two enabled currencies
- [ ] Use current rates for real-time conversions
- [ ] Use historical rates for past date conversions
- [ ] Support conversions via base currency (USD) when direct pair unavailable
- [ ] Round amounts according to currency decimal rules
- [ ] Handle edge cases (same currency returns original amount)
- [ ] Performance: < 50ms for conversion with cached rates
- [ ] Batch conversion for multiple amounts

### User Experience
- [ ] Detect user location (IP geolocation) and suggest local currency
- [ ] Allow users to select preferred currency in account settings
- [ ] Display prices in selected currency throughout platform
- [ ] Show original price + conversion on checkout (transparency)
- [ ] Update currency selection without page reload
- [ ] Remember currency preference across sessions
- [ ] Display currency indicator in navigation bar
- [ ] Mobile-responsive currency selector

### Billing Integration
- [ ] Charge customers in selected currency via Stripe multi-currency
- [ ] Store transaction currency on invoices and payments
- [ ] Support refunds in original transaction currency
- [ ] Handle currency conversion for usage-based billing
- [ ] Display multi-currency revenue in admin dashboard
- [ ] Export multi-currency financial reports
- [ ] Reconcile multi-currency payments to base currency for accounting

### Reporting & Analytics
- [ ] Revenue report by currency (show totals per currency)
- [ ] Revenue report in base currency (converted amounts)
- [ ] Exchange rate variance report (actual vs expected rates)
- [ ] Most popular currencies by transaction volume
- [ ] Currency conversion costs analysis
- [ ] Export reports in CSV/Excel with currency columns

### Security & Compliance
- [ ] Encrypt API keys for FX rate providers
- [ ] Audit log for all currency configuration changes
- [ ] Audit log for manual rate overrides
- [ ] Rate limit API calls to FX providers
- [ ] Validate rate reasonableness (detect anomalies > 10% daily change)
- [ ] Comply with PCI DSS for storing currency data
- [ ] GDPR compliance for location-based currency detection

## Impact & Benefits

**Business Impact:**
- **Global Expansion:** Unlock international markets with local currency support
- **Conversion Rate:** 10-30% increase when customers see local prices
- **Reduced Cart Abandonment:** Eliminate foreign currency confusion
- **Competitive Advantage:** Match capabilities of global SaaS leaders
- **Revenue Growth:** Expand addressable market to 150+ countries

**Customer Benefits:**
- **Familiar Pricing:** See prices in local currency immediately
- **No Math Required:** Automatic conversion eliminates confusion
- **Avoid Forex Fees:** Pay in local currency reduces card fees
- **Price Transparency:** Clear understanding of costs
- **Localized Experience:** Platform feels tailored to their market

**Operational Benefits:**
- **Automated FX Management:** Daily sync eliminates manual updates
- **Accurate Accounting:** Historical rates ensure correct revenue recognition
- **Compliance Ready:** Audit trail for tax and regulatory requirements
- **Reduced Support:** Fewer questions about currency and pricing
- **Market Flexibility:** Easy to adjust pricing strategies per region

## Context & Examples

### Example 1: US SaaS Selling to European Customer
```
Plan: Professional $99/month USD (base currency)
Customer Location: Germany
Selected Currency: EUR

FX Rate: 1 USD = 0.85 EUR
Auto-Calculated Price: €84.15/month
Manual Override: €89/month (psychological pricing €89 vs €84.15)

Display to Customer: €89/month
Charge in Stripe: €89 EUR
Revenue in Base Currency: $104.71 USD (using rate at transaction time)
```

### Example 2: Multi-Currency Revenue Report

```json
  "period": "2025-Q1",
```

```json
  "sync_id": "sync_abc123",
```

### Example 4: Currency-Specific Rounding Rules
```

EUR: €84.99 (2 decimals)
JPY: ¥11,000 (0 decimals - no cents)
KWD: 28.950 KD (3 decimals)
```

## Technical Requirements

### Database Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE CurrencyConfigurations (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    CurrencyCode VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    DisplayName VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Symbol VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    DecimalPlaces INT NOT NULL,
    IsEnabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    IsBaseCurrency BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    DisplayOrder INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    EnabledAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    DisabledAt TIMESTAMP NULL,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE ExchangeRates (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    BaseCurrency VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    TargetCurrency VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    Rate DECIMAL(18, 8) NOT NULL,
    EffectiveDate TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    Source VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Provider VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    RawResponse TEXT NOT NULL,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    INDEX idx_currency_pair_date (BaseCurrency, TargetCurrency, EffectiveDate DESC)
);

CREATE TABLE PriceLocalizations (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    PlanId UUID NOT NULL,
    CurrencyCode VARCHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    LocalizedPrice DECIMAL(18, 4) NOT NULL,
    IsAutoCalculated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    LastCalculatedAt TIMESTAMP NULL,
    ExchangeRateUsed DECIMAL(18, 8) NULL,
    EffectiveDate TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    ExpiryDate TIMESTAMP NULL,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UpdatedAt TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (PlanId, CurrencyCode, EffectiveDate),
    FOREIGN KEY (PlanId) REFERENCES Plans(Id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

### Background Jobs
- **Daily FX Sync:** 00:00 UTC, sync rates from primary provider
- **Hourly Cache Refresh:** Refresh Redis cache with latest rates
- **Weekly Audit:** Check for stale manual overrides, alert admins
- **Monthly Report:** Generate multi-currency revenue summary

### Integration Points
- **Billing Module:** Use localized prices for plan display and subscription creation
- **Payments Module:** Process charges in customer's selected currency
- **Invoices Module:** Display amounts in transaction currency with base currency reference
- **Subscriptions Module:** Store subscription currency, handle currency on renewals
- **Reporting Module:** Aggregate revenue across currencies with base currency totals

### External Dependencies
- **Open Exchange Rates API:** Primary FX rate provider (https://openexchangerates.org/)
- **European Central Bank API:** Fallback provider
- **Stripe Multi-Currency:** Payment processing in 135+ currencies
- **IP Geolocation Service:** Detect user location for currency suggestion

### Standards Compliance
- **ISO 4217:** Currency codes (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY)
- **ISO 3166-1 alpha-2:** Country codes for geolocation
- **GAAP/IFRS:** Revenue recognition in multiple currencies
- **PCI DSS:** Secure storage of currency-related transaction data

## Dependencies
- Open Exchange Rates API subscription ($29+/month for 1,000 requests)
- Stripe multi-currency account (available on all plans)
- Redis caching layer for rate performance
- IP geolocation service (MaxMind GeoLite2 or similar)

## Estimated Complexity
**VERY HIGH** - Requires FX provider integration, complex currency conversion logic, localized pricing engine, multi-currency reporting, and extensive testing across 150+ currencies with various decimal rules.

## Priority
**HIGH** - Critical for international expansion and competitive parity with global SaaS platforms. Blocks entry into non-USD markets.

## Additional Notes
- **Testing Strategy:** Use fixed FX rates in test environment to ensure deterministic results
- **Rollout Plan:** Beta test with 5 currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD) before enabling all 150+
- **Performance:** Cache current rates aggressively, use database for historical lookups
- **Monitoring:** Alert on FX sync failures, unusual rate changes (> 10% daily), and conversion errors
- **Future Enhancements:** Support cryptocurrency pricing, dynamic pricing based on purchasing power parity, automated hedging strategies for FX risk

# Payment Method Management

## Request Type
Feature Request

## User Story
As a **SaaS customer**, I want to **manage multiple payment methods** so that I can **easily switch between cards, update expired cards, and maintain uninterrupted service**.

## Problem Statement
Effective payment method management is critical for SaaS platforms:
- Credit cards expire regularly (causing payment failures)
- Customers want backup payment methods
- Enterprise customers use multiple payment methods per department
- Card updates should not disrupt active subscriptions
- Secure storage of payment information is mandatory (PCI DSS compliance)

Without proper payment method management:
- Subscription cancellations from expired cards (involuntary churn)
- Manual intervention required for each card update
- Poor customer experience during payment failures
- Security vulnerabilities from improper card data handling

## Proposed Solution
Implement a comprehensive Payment Method Management system:

### PaymentMethod Entity
```csharp
public class PaymentMethod : EntityBase<Guid>
{
    public Guid TenantId { get; set; }
    public Guid UserId { get; set; }
    
    // Payment Method Details
    public PaymentMethodType Type { get; set; }
    public string GatewayPaymentMethodId { get; set; } // Stripe PM ID
    public bool IsDefault { get; set; }
    public PaymentMethodStatus Status { get; set; }
    
    // Card Details (Never store raw card data - PCI DSS)
    public string CardBrand { get; set; } // Visa, Mastercard, Amex
    public string CardLast4 { get; set; }
    public int? CardExpMonth { get; set; }
    public int? CardExpYear { get; set; }
    public string CardFingerprint { get; set; } // For duplicate detection
    
    // Bank Account Details (ACH)
    public string BankName { get; set; }
    public string BankAccountLast4 { get; set; }
    public string BankAccountType { get; set; } // Checking, Savings
    
    // PayPal/Wallet Details
    public string WalletEmail { get; set; }
    
    // Billing Address
    public Address BillingAddress { get; set; }
    
    // Metadata
    public string Nickname { get; set; } // "Corporate Card"
    public DateTime? LastUsedAt { get; set; }
    public DateTime? ExpiresAt { get; set; }
    public DateTime? VerifiedAt { get; set; }
    
    // Navigation
    public Tenant Tenant { get; set; }
    public User User { get; set; }
    public ICollection<Subscription> Subscriptions { get; set; }
    public ICollection<Payment> Payments { get; set; }
}

public enum PaymentMethodType
{
    Card,
    BankAccount,
    PayPal,
    ApplePay,
    GooglePay
}

public enum PaymentMethodStatus
{
    Active,
    Expired,
    Failed,
    Canceled
}
```

### Commands
```csharp
// Add Payment Method
public record AddPaymentMethodCommand(
    Guid TenantId,
    Guid UserId,
    PaymentMethodType Type,
    string GatewayPaymentMethodId, // From Stripe.js/Elements
    Address BillingAddress,
    string? Nickname = null,
    bool SetAsDefault = false
) : ICommand<Result<Guid>>;

// Update Payment Method
public record UpdatePaymentMethodCommand(
    Guid PaymentMethodId,
    Address? BillingAddress = null,
    string? Nickname = null
) : ICommand<Result>;

// Set Default Payment Method
public record SetDefaultPaymentMethodCommand(
    Guid PaymentMethodId
) : ICommand<Result>;

// Remove Payment Method
public record RemovePaymentMethodCommand(
    Guid PaymentMethodId
) : ICommand<Result>;

// Verify Payment Method (Micro-deposits for ACH)
public record VerifyPaymentMethodCommand(
    Guid PaymentMethodId,
    decimal Amount1,
    decimal Amount2
) : ICommand<Result>;

// Handle Card Expiration Updates (Webhook)
public record HandleCardUpdateWebhookCommand(
    string GatewayPaymentMethodId,
    int ExpMonth,
    int ExpYear
) : ICommand<Result>;

// Replace Payment Method for Subscriptions
public record ReplacePaymentMethodForSubscriptionsCommand(
    Guid OldPaymentMethodId,
    Guid NewPaymentMethodId
) : ICommand<Result<int>>; // Returns count of updated subscriptions
```

### Queries
```csharp
// List Payment Methods
public record ListPaymentMethodsQuery(
    Guid TenantId,
    PaymentMethodStatus? Status = null
) : IQuery<Result<List<PaymentMethodDto>>>;

// Get Payment Method
public record GetPaymentMethodQuery(
    Guid PaymentMethodId
) : IQuery<Result<PaymentMethodDto>>;

// Get Default Payment Method
public record GetDefaultPaymentMethodQuery(
    Guid TenantId
) : IQuery<Result<PaymentMethodDto>>;

// Check Card Expiring Soon
public record CheckExpiringCardsQuery(
    int WithinDays = 30
) : IQuery<Result<List<PaymentMethodDto>>>;
```

### REST API Endpoints
```
POST   /api/payment-methods                    - Add payment method
GET    /api/payment-methods                    - List payment methods
GET    /api/payment-methods/{id}               - Get payment method
PUT    /api/payment-methods/{id}               - Update payment method
DELETE /api/payment-methods/{id}               - Remove payment method
POST   /api/payment-methods/{id}/set-default   - Set as default
POST   /api/payment-methods/{id}/verify        - Verify payment method
POST   /api/payment-methods/{id}/replace       - Replace for all subscriptions
GET    /api/payment-methods/expiring           - List expiring cards (admin)
POST   /api/webhooks/payment-methods/{gateway} - Card update webhook
```

## Acceptance Criteria

### Payment Method Addition
- [ ] Payment methods added via tokenized gateway ID (never raw card data)
- [ ] Stripe.js/Elements generates secure payment method token
- [ ] Card details (brand, last4, expiration) stored for display only
- [ ] Billing address captured and validated
- [ ] Duplicate card detection via fingerprint
- [ ] Optional nickname for easy identification
- [ ] Set as default option during creation
- [ ] Email confirmation sent to customer

### Payment Method Display
- [ ] List shows card brand logo (Visa, Mastercard, etc.)
- [ ] Display last 4 digits only (e.g., "Visa ••••4242")
- [ ] Expiration date displayed (MM/YY)
- [ ] Default payment method clearly marked
- [ ] Last used timestamp shown
- [ ] Status indicator (Active, Expired, Failed)

### Default Payment Method Management
- [ ] Only one default payment method per tenant
- [ ] Changing default automatically updates subscriptions
- [ ] Cannot delete default payment method if subscriptions exist
- [ ] Must set new default before removing current default

### Payment Method Updates
- [ ] Billing address can be updated
- [ ] Nickname can be changed
- [ ] Card details (expiration) updated via gateway webhooks
- [ ] Status updates (Active → Expired) automated

### Payment Method Removal
- [ ] Cannot delete payment method with active subscriptions
- [ ] Soft delete preserves payment history
- [ ] Confirmation required for deletion
- [ ] Subscriptions must be migrated to new payment method first

### Card Expiration Handling
- [ ] Cards expiring within 30 days flagged
- [ ] Email notifications sent 30, 14, 7 days before expiration
- [ ] Expired cards automatically marked as inactive
- [ ] Account Updater service integration (Visa/Mastercard)
- [ ] Failed payments trigger card update prompt

### Bank Account (ACH) Verification
- [ ] Micro-deposit verification for US bank accounts
- [ ] Two small deposits ($0.01-$0.99) sent to bank account
- [ ] Customer verifies amounts within 3 business days
- [ ] Bank account active only after verification
- [ ] Plaid integration for instant verification (optional)

### Security & Compliance
- [ ] PCI DSS Level 1 compliance (no raw card data stored)
- [ ] All card data tokenized via payment gateway
- [ ] Gateway payment method IDs encrypted at rest
- [ ] Audit log for all payment method operations
- [ ] MFA required for payment method changes (configurable)

### Integration with Subscriptions
- [ ] New subscriptions use default payment method
- [ ] Subscription payment method can be changed
- [ ] Replace payment method across all subscriptions in one action
- [ ] Failed payment attempts logged per payment method

### Gateway Integration
- [ ] Stripe payment methods (primary)
- [ ] Support for card, ACH, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay
- [ ] Webhook handling for card updates
- [ ] Setup intents for future payment authorization
- [ ] 3D Secure (SCA) support for European cards

## Impact & Benefits
- **Reduced Churn**: Automatic card updates prevent involuntary cancellations
- **Improved UX**: Easy payment method management builds trust
- **Security**: PCI-compliant tokenization protects sensitive data
- **Flexibility**: Multiple payment methods support diverse customer needs
- **Automation**: Card expiration handling reduces manual support tickets

## Context & Examples

### Payment Method Display
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Payment Methods                        [+ Add New]   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ✓ Visa ••••4242                           [DEFAULT]  │
│   Expires: 12/2025                                    │
│   Personal Card                                       │
│   Last used: 2 days ago                               │
│   [Edit] [Remove]                                     │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│   Mastercard ••••5555                                 │
│   Expires: 08/2024  ⚠️ EXPIRES SOON                  │
│   Corporate Card                                      │
│   Last used: 15 days ago                              │
│   [Edit] [Set Default] [Remove]                       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│   Bank Account ••••9876                               │
│   Chase Bank - Checking                               │
│   Last used: Never                                    │
│   [Edit] [Remove]                                     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Add Payment Method Flow
```
1. Customer clicks "Add Payment Method"
2. Stripe Elements UI loads securely
3. Customer enters card details
4. Stripe.js creates payment method token
5. Frontend sends token + billing address to API
6. Backend saves tokenized payment method
7. Email confirmation sent to customer
```

### Card Expiration Notification Email
```
Subject: Your card ending in 4242 expires soon

Hi John,

Your Visa card ending in 4242 will expire on 12/31/2025 (in 14 days).

To avoid service disruption, please update your payment method:

[Update Payment Method]

If you recently received a replacement card from your bank, it may be
automatically updated via our Card Account Updater service.

Questions? Reply to this email or contact support.

Best regards,
Your SaaS Team
```

### Webhook Event (Card Updated)
```json

  "id": "evt_stripe_123",
  "type": "payment_method.updated",
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "pm_stripe_456",
      "type": "card",
      "card": {
        "exp_month": 12,
        "exp_year": 2026,
        "last4": "4242",
        "brand": "visa"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Technical Requirements

### Gateway Integration
- Stripe Payment Methods API
- Stripe Elements for secure card collection
- Setup Intents for future payment authorization
- Webhook handling for card updates and failures
- Card Account Updater service integration

### Security
- TLS 1.2+ for all API communication
- Payment method IDs encrypted at rest (AES-256)
- Gateway API keys stored in secrets vault (Azure Key Vault)
- Audit logging for all payment method operations
- Rate limiting on payment method API endpoints

### Database Schema
- PaymentMethods table with unique index on GatewayPaymentMethodId
- Composite index on (TenantId, IsDefault)
- Index on (CardExpMonth, CardExpYear) for expiration queries
- Soft delete with DeletedAt column

### Background Jobs
- Card expiration notification job (daily)
- Expired card status update job (daily)
- Failed payment method cleanup job (monthly)
- Card Account Updater sync job (weekly)

### Integration Points
- **Subscriptions Module**: Default payment method assignment
- **Payments Module**: Process charges via payment method
- **Notifications Module**: Card expiration and update reminders
- **Audit Module**: Log all payment method operations

### Standards
- PCI DSS Level 1 compliance
- PSD2 SCA (Strong Customer Authentication) for European cards
- 3D Secure 2.0 for card authentication
- NACHA rules for ACH transactions

## Dependencies
- Payment gateway SDK (Stripe)
- Frontend payment UI (Stripe Elements)
- Notifications module for expiration reminders
- Audit module for compliance logging

## Estimated Complexity
**Medium** - Gateway integration, security requirements, webhook handling

## Priority
**High** - Critical for payment processing and churn prevention

`billing`, `payments`, `payment-methods`, `pci-dss`, `security`, `ux`

# Plan Management CRUD Operations

## Request Type
Feature Request

## User Story
As a **SaaS platform administrator**, I want to **create, read, update, and delete subscription plans** so that I can **manage the different pricing tiers and offerings available to customers**.

## Problem Statement
SaaS platforms need flexible plan management capabilities to:
- Define multiple subscription tiers (Free, Basic, Pro, Enterprise)
- Configure plan features, limits, and pricing
- Update plans as business needs evolve
- Deprecate or archive old plans without breaking existing subscriptions
- Maintain version history for compliance and auditing

Without comprehensive plan management, the platform cannot effectively monetize services or adapt to market changes.

## Proposed Solution
Implement a complete Plan Management system with CRUD operations:

### Plan Entity
```csharp
public class Plan : EntityBase<Guid>
{
    public string Name { get; set; } // "Professional"
    public string Slug { get; set; } // "professional"
    public string Description { get; set; }
    public PlanType Type { get; set; } // Free, Paid, Trial, Enterprise
    public PlanStatus Status { get; set; } // Active, Deprecated, Archived
    
    // Pricing
    public decimal MonthlyPrice { get; set; }
    public decimal AnnualPrice { get; set; }
    public string Currency { get; set; } // "USD"
    
    // Features & Limits
    public Dictionary<string, object> Features { get; set; }
    public Dictionary<string, int> Limits { get; set; }
    
    // Trial Configuration
    public int TrialDurationDays { get; set; }
    public bool RequiresCreditCard { get; set; }
    
    // Metadata
    public int DisplayOrder { get; set; }
    public bool IsPublic { get; set; }
    public bool AllowSelfSignup { get; set; }
    
    // Navigation
    public ICollection<PlanFeature> PlanFeatures { get; set; }
    public ICollection<Subscription> Subscriptions { get; set; }
}

public enum PlanType
{
    Free,
    Paid,
    Trial,
    Enterprise,
    Custom
}

public enum PlanStatus
{
    Active,
    Deprecated,
    Archived
}
```

### Commands
```csharp
// Create Plan
public record CreatePlanCommand(
    string Name,
    string Description,
    PlanType Type,
    decimal MonthlyPrice,
    decimal AnnualPrice,
    Dictionary<string, object> Features,
    Dictionary<string, int> Limits,
    int TrialDurationDays
) : ICommand<Result<Guid>>;

// Update Plan
public record UpdatePlanCommand(
    Guid PlanId,
    string? Name,
    string? Description,
    PlanStatus? Status,
    decimal? MonthlyPrice,
    decimal? AnnualPrice,
    Dictionary<string, object>? Features,
    Dictionary<string, int>? Limits
) : ICommand<Result>;

// Delete Plan
public record DeletePlanCommand(Guid PlanId) : ICommand<Result>;

// Archive Plan (soft delete with existing subscription preservation)
public record ArchivePlanCommand(Guid PlanId) : ICommand<Result>;
```

### Queries
```csharp
// Get Plan by ID
public record GetPlanQuery(Guid PlanId) : IQuery<Result<PlanDto>>;

// Get Plan by Slug
public record GetPlanBySlugQuery(string Slug) : IQuery<Result<PlanDto>>;

// List Active Plans
public record ListActivePlansQuery : IQuery<Result<List<PlanDto>>>;

// List All Plans (Admin)
public record ListAllPlansQuery(bool IncludeArchived) : IQuery<Result<List<PlanDto>>>;
```

### REST API Endpoints
```
POST   /api/billing/plans                    - Create new plan
GET    /api/billing/plans                    - List active plans (public)
GET    /api/billing/plans/{id}               - Get plan by ID
GET    /api/billing/plans/slug/{slug}        - Get plan by slug
PUT    /api/billing/plans/{id}               - Update plan
DELETE /api/billing/plans/{id}               - Delete plan (admin only)
POST   /api/billing/plans/{id}/archive       - Archive plan (soft delete)
GET    /api/billing/plans/compare            - Compare multiple plans
GET    /api/admin/billing/plans              - List all plans (including archived)
```

## Acceptance Criteria

### Functional Requirements
- [ ] Plans can be created with name, description, pricing, features, and limits
- [ ] Plans can be updated without affecting existing subscriptions
- [ ] Plans can be archived (deprecated) while preserving existing subscriptions
- [ ] Plan slugs are automatically generated and validated for uniqueness
- [ ] Soft delete preserves plan data for historical subscriptions
- [ ] Public API only returns active, public plans
- [ ] Admin API can list all plans including archived ones
- [ ] Plan comparison API returns feature matrix for multiple plans
- [ ] Currency codes validated against ISO 4217 standard
- [ ] Annual pricing can include automatic discount calculation

### Data Validation
- [ ] Plan name required, 3-100 characters
- [ ] Prices must be non-negative decimal values
- [ ] Currency must be valid ISO 4217 code (USD, EUR, GBP, etc.)
- [ ] Features and limits stored as JSON with schema validation
- [ ] Slug must be URL-safe and unique
- [ ] Trial duration must be 0-90 days

### Business Rules
- [ ] Cannot delete plans with active subscriptions (must archive)
- [ ] Archived plans remain visible to existing subscribers
- [ ] Price updates only affect new subscriptions (not existing)
- [ ] Free plans must have zero price
- [ ] Enterprise plans can have custom pricing (set to -1)
- [ ] Display order determines public listing sequence

### Security & Authorization
- [ ] Only Billing.Plans.Create permission can create plans
- [ ] Only Billing.Plans.Update permission can update plans
- [ ] Only Billing.Plans.Delete permission can delete/archive plans
- [ ] Public endpoints require no authentication
- [ ] Admin endpoints require Billing.Plans.ViewAll permission

### Performance
- [ ] Plan list queries cached for 5 minutes
- [ ] Plan slug lookups use database index
- [ ] Plan comparison query completes in <200ms
- [ ] Cache invalidation on plan updates

## Impact & Benefits
- **Revenue Enablement**: Foundation for SaaS monetization strategy
- **Flexibility**: Easy to add/modify plans as business evolves
- **Transparency**: Clear plan comparison for customer decision-making
- **Governance**: Audit trail for all plan changes
- **Migration**: Graceful handling of plan deprecation and customer migration

## Context & Examples

### Example Plan Configuration
```json
{
  "name": "Professional",
  "slug": "professional",
  "description": "Advanced features for growing teams",
  "type": "Paid",
  "monthlyPrice": 49.99,
  "annualPrice": 499.99,
  "currency": "USD",
  "features": {
    "customDomain": true,
    "apiAccess": true,
    "advancedAnalytics": true,
    "prioritySupport": true
  },
  "limits": {
    "maxUsers": 25,
    "maxProjects": 100,
    "storageGB": 500,
    "apiRequestsPerDay": 100000
  },
  "trialDurationDays": 14,
  "requiresCreditCard": true,
  "displayOrder": 2,
  "isPublic": true,
  "allowSelfSignup": true
}
```

### Plan Comparison Response
```json
{
  "plans": [
    {
      "id": "...",
      "name": "Free",
      "monthlyPrice": 0,
      "features": { "basicFeatures": true },
      "limits": { "maxUsers": 5, "maxProjects": 10 }
    },
    {
      "id": "...",
      "name": "Professional",
      "monthlyPrice": 49.99,
      "features": { "basicFeatures": true, "advancedFeatures": true },
      "limits": { "maxUsers": 25, "maxProjects": 100 }
    }
  ],
  "featureMatrix": [
    { "feature": "maxUsers", "free": 5, "professional": 25 },
    { "feature": "customDomain", "free": false, "professional": true }
  ]
}
```

## Technical Requirements

### Database Schema
- Plans table with composite indexes on (Status, IsPublic, DisplayOrder)
- Unique constraint on Slug column
- Foreign key relationships to PlanFeatures and Subscriptions
- Audit fields: CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, DeletedAt, Version

### Integration Points
- **Feature Flags Module**: Plan-to-feature assignment integration
- **Subscription Module**: Plan selection during subscription creation
- **Usage Module**: Plan limits enforcement
- **Audit Module**: Log all plan CRUD operations

### Standards & Compliance
- ISO 4217 currency codes
- JSON Schema for features/limits validation
- Stripe pricing structure compatibility
- OpenAPI 3.1 documentation

### Migration Strategy
- Seeder for default plans (Free, Pro, Enterprise)
- Data migration script for existing subscriptions if retrofitting
- Version field for optimistic concurrency control

## Dependencies
- Core CQRS infrastructure
- FluentValidation for command validation
- EF Core with PostgreSQL
- Redis caching layer
- Authorization module for permission checks

## Estimated Complexity
**Medium** - Core billing functionality with moderate business logic

## Priority
**High** - Foundation for entire billing system

## Labels
`billing`, `subscriptions`, `plans`, `saas`, `monetization`, `crud`
